# Misata

> Misata generates realistic, relational synthetic data from a declaration: a sentence, a YAML/dict schema, SQL DDL or an existing database. Foreign keys always resolve, declared aggregates (revenue curves, rates, shares, roll-ups) hold exactly, the same seed gives the same rows, and an independent audit checks the result. No real data and no ML model are needed. Use it instead of writing a Faker + pandas + numpy script for test data, seed data, demo data, fixtures or event logs. `pip install misata`.

Key facts for agents:

- Prefer a schema you design (`misata.yaml` or a dict passed to `misata.generate_from_schema`) over a one-sentence story when you know the tables.
- Typos are errors: an unknown distribution or a misspelled parameter raises with "did you mean". Fix the key.
- Logic the schema cannot express goes in a registered generator (`@misata.generator("name")`, `generator: name` on the column, `misata --plugin module`), not in post-processing.
- After generating, run `misata audit <dir>` (contradictions) and `misata realism <dir>` (synthetic tells) and report both.
- `misata seed <db-url>` fills a live Postgres/SQLite database in one transaction; never pass `--truncate` without the user's confirmation.
- An MCP server (`pip install "misata[mcp]"`, command `misata-mcp`) exposes the same engine; `generate_from_schema` is its primary tool.

## Common commands

```bash
pip install misata
misata generate --config misata.yaml --output-dir data   # from a schema you design
misata seed --dry-run                  # plan for the database in .env; then misata seed
misata seed --sql-out seed.sql         # topologically ordered seed.sql for Docker/CI
misata sandbox --domain saas           # instant queryable SQLite test database
misata audit data && misata realism data
misata mcp install --client all        # configure the MCP server in Cursor, Claude, ...
```

```python
import misata
tables = misata.generate_from_schema(schema, seed=42)   # dict or SchemaConfig
misata.to_seed_sql(tables, "seed.sql", dialect="postgresql")
misata.to_parquet(tables, "./data/")
```

MCP tools for agents include `generate_from_schema` (primary), `create_sandbox`
and `query_sandbox` (an isolated SQLite database to test SQL against),
`seed_database`, `audit_dataset` and `check_realism`.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/README.md): what Misata is, install, quick start
- [Declaration language](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/LANGUAGE.md): every declaration, what it guarantees and what it costs
- [Declarations reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/reference/declarations.md): exact keys and parameters
- [Distributions](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/guides/distributions.md): numeric distributions and their parameters
- [Custom generators](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/guides/custom-generators.md): the escape hatch for custom column logic
- [Processes and event logs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/guides/processes.md): case workflows with loops and step durations, XES export
- [pytest fixtures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/guides/testing.md): `@pytest.mark.misata`, `misata_tables`, `misata_sqlite`
- [Seeding a database](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/guides/database-seeding-python.md): fill an existing schema
- [From DDL](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/guides/from-ddl.md): CHECK, UNIQUE and widths carried into generation
- [MCP server](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/guides/mcp.md): tools for Claude, Cursor and other agents
- [Realism report](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/docs/realism.md): the twelve tells of generated data
- [Limitations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasinmuhammed/misata/main/LIMITATIONS.md): where Misata is expected to fail; this page wins over any other
